basis: 66 chronological sequence pages of the exact muted phone preview, sampled at 5 frames per second (frames 0 to 1963, 65.433 s including credits from 60.6 s). Viewed from movie-derived images only, with no playback or listening. Motion between samples is unproven.

blocking_defects.defect: In the s3 menu-tap medium shot (19.2 to 20.4 s) a seated guest appears with an oversized foreground hand holding the phone. A second, long arm reaches from the frame edge to tap the Chow mein row. Neither limb joins the guest's body, and the hand is out of scale with the guest. The n3b order action is performed by detached, stretched limbs rather than by the person shown. This fails contact_and_consequence and continuity, and the viewer sees a broken figure at the moment the order is placed.

In s10 stand-wide (53.8 to 56.7 s) the only action for 'So software now takes the order' is a tiny order card and slip on the panel (54.4 to 55.2 s) in a wide room, then a static hold from about 55.4 to 56.6 s. At phone size the first half of the answer reads as an unchanged room. This fails the finished_art floor for tiny performed actions.

closing_answer.observed: The ending answers the opening question on the rig the film built. The printed Chow mein ticket hangs above the jar, which carries owner says and no record shown tags, so the order came through software and the tip claim rests on the owner's word without a resolved outcome being invented.

finished_art.observed: Most frames are finished. Two performed actions fail: in the s3 medium shot (19.2 to 20.4 s) detached, scale-mismatched limbs make the order tap, and in the s10 wide shot (54.4 to 56.6 s) the panel's order action is tiny and is followed by a static hold.

first_frame.observed: The film opens on an overhead floor plan. The door swings shut from about 0.5 s and a footprint trail leads from the host stand out the door by 2.4 s, a visible change well before 1.5 s. The lower half of the plan is empty.

pace.observed: There are no holds near 5 s. The longest observed static intervals are about 2 s on the empty storefront sign frame (8.8 to 10.8 s), about 1.8 s on the rule card (40.8 to 42.6 s) and about 1.2 s in the s10 wide shot (55.4 to 56.6 s). Rewards land within 4 s of one another across the story.

performed_turn.observed: The folder slides in beside the rule card (46.8 to 47.2 s), opens in close-up (47.4 to 47.8 s), and its single box stays blank with a question mark (48.4 to 48.8 s). That puts the unknown tip credit on screen before the closing tags.

shot_variety.observed: Overhead (floor plan, table, desk, pass, rule card), medium (stand, panel, seated guest, pass), close (pad, jar, folder), wide (storefront, pass, room) and detail (tag, Pay, flame, final tags) framings alternate. No shot exceeds 5 s.

visual_progression.observed: Each scene adds a new state on recurring objects. The empty station and ringing phone lead to the empty sign frame and the lit panel, then to scan, tap and Paid. The paid token reaches the printer, followed by the ticket and flare. Next come the ledger with tag and stamp, coins into the jar, the rule card with lit cook line, the folder with its blank box, the hesitant scan with the quote, and finally the tagged jar under the printed ticket.

closing_payoff.observed: At 56.8 s a medium pass shows printer, ticket and jar, and the owner says tag swings onto the jar at 57.0 to 57.8 s. A detail from 58.4 s holds the printer with its Chow mein ticket above the full jar. The no record shown tag swings in and settles under the owner says tag at 59.0 to 59.8 s, with both tags large and legible until the cut to credits at 60.6 s.

contact_and_consequence.observed: Strong contact chains exist elsewhere: the paid token travels into the printer, the lamp turns red at 25.6 s, the ticket rises and the pour flares the wok at 26.6 to 27.8 s, and coins slide across the pass into the jar at 35.2 to 36.6 s. In s3 at 19.2 to 20.4 s, however, the tap on the menu is made by a long arm from the frame edge while a seated guest holds an oversized hand. Neither limb belongs to the guest, so the claimed customer action is not performed by a credible person.

subject_recognition.observed: The restaurant room, host stand phone, apron, empty window sign frame, Haniya host panel with AI host tag, table code card, phone menu with the Chow mein row, printer, ticket, wok, ledger card, rule card, folder, quote card and tip jar are each recognizable at phone size. The exception is the s10 order card on the panel in the wide shot (54.4 to 55.2 s), which is very small.

surface_finish.observed: The picture is clean, flat authored illustration throughout: legible tags and cards, consistent warm palette and stable linework. The single smeared hand fragment at 50.8 s is held as unresolved until native inspection and is not counted here. The s3 limb scale is recorded under contact_and_consequence.

blocking_defects.defect: The s3 order tap (19.2 to 20.4 s) is performed by detached, scale-mismatched limbs that don't belong to the seated guest shown.
The s10 answer action for 'software now takes the order' (54.4 to 56.6 s) is a tiny card and slip in a wide room, followed by a static hold.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: From above, the server's footprints leave as the door shuts and the phone rings at an empty stand. No job ad goes up, and a host panel named Haniya lights. A guest scans, taps and pays, and the paid mark is followed into the printer, which prints the Chow mein ticket as the wok flares. The owner's $9,650 figure is stamped as his own count beside a bare clip. Coins cross the pass into the jar under a FOX 26 tag. The federal rule card lights the cook line, but the restaurant folder's box stays blank. A customer hesitates at the code. The jar ends under owner says and no record shown tags beside the printed ticket.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening asks who takes the order now that the server is gone. The ending shows the order printed by the system above a jar whose tip claim carries owner says and no record shown, which answers the question within the source limits without inventing an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: The 19.05 s cut from the overhead code-scan to the medium menu-tap introduces a seated guest whose body doesn't own the phone hand or the tapping arm.

strongest_frame: s4 paid-line push-in into ticket-print and wok flare, 24.6 to 27.8 s.

unresolved_findings.finding: At frame 1524 (rechecked) the phone has been set down, and the withdrawing hand shows as a smeared, jagged-edged orange-brown fragment below the table edge and the caption band. It appears in one sample during motion. Whether it is a render smear or a sampled transient visible at playback speed is unproven, and it needs native-frame inspection. It is not counted as a blocker here.
The Pay and Paid detail (21.4 to 22.8 s) shows no holding hand, a continuity jump from the preceding hands. This is noted only.

weakest_frame: s3 menu-tap medium, 19.2 to 20.4 s. A seated guest has an oversized foreground hand while a separate long arm taps the menu, so neither limb connects to the guest.
